name: Home Assistant
insteadOf: Google Home / Apple HomeKit / Amazon Alexa
hook: The local brain of your smart home — one dashboard for thousands of devices, no cloud required.
bullets: Unifies lights, cameras, sensors, and 2,000+ integrations in one dashboard
Automations run locally — your smart home keeps working when the internet goes down
Works with Zigbee, Z-Wave, Matter, MQTT, ESPHome, and big-name brands
Free and open source, with companion apps for Android and iOS
benefits: Google Home and Alexa without shipping your data to Big Tech
Your devices keep working offline — no outage can brick your home
Mix cheap sensors and disparate brands that were never meant to talk
Automate everything from presence to energy use with one rule engine
setupSteps: Install Home Assistant OS on a Raspberry Pi, mini PC, or NAS (or run it in Docker)
Open the dashboard and add your devices through Discover or an integration
Build a dashboard with the drag-and-drop cards you care about
Add automations to react to time, presence, device state, and events
details: Home Assistant is the most popular open-source home automation platform — a local 'brain' that unifies thousands of smart devices and services into a single dashboard and automation engine. It talks to lights, switches, sensors, cameras, thermostats, media players, and 2,000+ integrations from brands like Philips Hue, Zigbee, Z-Wave, MQTT, ESPHome, and Matter, and it runs entirely on your own hardware so automations keep working even when the internet goes down. Beyond dashboards, its UI- and YAML-driven automation engine can react to time, presence, device state, and events, and companion apps for Android and iOS add widgets, sensors, and notifications. It's free, open source (Apache-2.0), actively developed, and backed by the Open Home Foundation and a huge community of integration maintainers.
setup: Self-hosted (Raspberry Pi, mini PC, or NAS)
